name: Is partial pool removal risky because of future settling?

mainEntity.name: Does a partial in-ground pool removal settle over time, and how can homeowners reduce that risk?
mainEntity.text: Does a partial in-ground pool removal settle over time, and how can homeowners reduce that risk?

acceptedAnswer.text: Partial removal can be a practical option, but it carries a settlement risk if the fill is not placed and compacted correctly. The risk increases when the area will later support patios, retaining walls, garages, or additions. Even for landscaping, poor drainage can cause low spots, soft ground, or uneven lawn areas over time. Homeowners should ask whether the contractor compacts in lifts, uses clean fill, and documents the process. If future construction is possible, engineered fill is often worth considering. In Los Angeles neighborhoods with variable soils or hillside lots, settlement concerns are even more important. A lower upfront price is not always a better value if the site needs rework later. The safest decision depends on what the yard will be used for after demolition and how much weight the area will need to support.
acceptedAnswer.description: Partial pool removal can settle if the backfill is not compacted correctly or if the fill material and drainage are poor. The risk is higher when the old shell remains buried and the area is later used for heavy loads or structures. Proper compaction, good fill selection, and drainage planning reduce the chance of sinking.
